speaker_role: current admissions officers: Associate Dean of Admissions at Wake Forest University, and an international admissions representative at the University of Notre Dame
commercial_incentive: The Red Pen (a Mumbai-based paid college consulting company) hosts and promotes its own services around the webinar; the school reps' own content is not sales-driven
key_insights: Wake Forest students don't declare majors until second year; 89% double major or double minor; average class size is 24

Wake Forest offers a general (non-specialized) engineering degree combined with liberal arts, uncommon nationally, with reported 45% women (vs. ~10% nationally) and 35% students of color in the program
Wake Forest states it was the first top-30 university to go test-optional, over ten years before this recording

Notre Dame requires an intended major on application but doesn't require formal declaration until end of first year; direct-admit restrictions mainly apply to select programs like nursing and some engineering paths
At the time of this webinar, Notre Dame was 'test flexible' (not blind) for A-level/IB students but still required SAT/ACT for students from standard curricula like CBSE (subject tests not required)
Both schools said submitting or withholding test scores under test-optional policy doesn't inherently help or hurt, with officers emphasizing rigor and teacher input over raw scores

Notre Dame states it meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for admitted students who apply for aid at the time of application, and is need-aware for international admissions (so aid intent must be flagged upfront)
Wake Forest offers merit-based international scholarships; an alumni interview was cited as a way to raise visibility with the scholarship committee
specific_numbers_or_facts: Wake Forest: 89% double major/minor, average class size 24, 45% women in engineering (vs. ~10% nationally), 35% students of color in engineering, 75% study abroad (per Nikki McEntire)
Notre Dame: about 8,500 undergrads, students from 80 countries, 98% job placement within 6 months (99% by year end), 250+ alumni clubs worldwide (per Mary Devilliers)
notable_or_distinctive: Direct side-by-side comparison of two distinctive mid-sized selective universities answering identical audience questions, including candid discussion of COVID-era campus safety for international students stranded abroad.
reliability_notes: Recorded during early COVID-19 (2020); testing-policy and campus-operations details are specific to that period and likely outdated; numeric claims are officer-stated without external verification.
